rows.claim: Every field-emitting component must expose (component, input values) -> handle as a plain, pure, public function
rows.note: No field-emitting component ships in src/ and nothing enforces the obligation; the example components are in Flight.jl, outside this repo.

rows.claim: The field-emitting component's swept output stage must be a one-line call to the value-level constructor, never the other way round
rows.note: Authoring obligation on a shipped component; no such component in src/ to inspect.

rows.claim: The condition math of §14.1 can construct, outside any sweep, bit-for-bit the same handle the sweep produces from the same root-input values
rows.note: Depends on a field-emitting component that this repo does not ship.

rows.claim: The value-level constructor is a shipped component's obligation, not something a consumer can retrofit
rows.note: Same as above; a design rule on shipped components, not checkable in src/.

rows.claim: For bulk-data components the obligation is only that the query math be reachable as a plain function
rows.note: No bulk-data field-emitting component in src/.

rows.claim: `x_init` holding a store and no `x_deriv` method, or `s_init` holding a store and no `s_update` method, is `StoreWithoutUpdate`
rows.fix: `x_init` holding a store with neither `x_deriv` nor `s_update`, or `s_init` holding a store with neither, is `StoreWithoutUpdate`. An `x_init` store beside only `s_update`, or an `s_init` store beside only `x_deriv`, is `DeclarationOnWrongTier`.
rows.note: The code raises StoreWithoutUpdate only when neither update law exists (assembly.jl:743, declare.jl:70). The spec's later mixed-case sentence (line 3511-3513) already says DeclarationOnWrongTier for these.

rows.claim: `x_projection` is continuous-only and its disagreement is checked with the other tier-implying declarations in the structure step
rows.fix: `m_init` and `state_events` vote in the structure step. `x_projection` on a discrete primitive is `DeclarationOnWrongTier` (`:continuous_only`) raised later, in the stage-2 probe of the nominal evaluation, and carries no announced tier.
rows.note: `classify_tier` casts no `x_projection` vote (assembly.jl:728-735); build.jl:1154-1161 raises it, and the carrier already holds the Structure (probe:154).
Log and trace export path not traced.

rows.claim: The typo'd wire's message reads "no input `throtle`; did you mean `throttle`?"
rows.fix: A typo'd wire (`:throtle`) is a build error at the connection, `UnknownPort`: "names no `throtle` on `c` — its faces are throttle, out". The unfed `throttle` input is also reported, as `UnconnectedInput`.
rows.note: The message lists the endpoint's faces and offers no nearest-name suggestion; the build also reports the left-unfed input (no cascade suppression, build.jl:787).

rows.claim: `Group((; plant = Plant(), ctrl = PID(kp = 2.0)); local_wires = (…))` builds a `PID` with keyword `kp`
rows.note: The library `PID` keyword is `Kp` (capital K); `kp` is a MethodError. `Plant` is a placeholder.

rows.claim: Abstract container element types follow the same concreteness discipline as plain fields
rows.note: Guidance on authoring; no code check of element concreteness exists.

rows.claim: Declaring two transparent containers on one type is a declaration error
rows.fix: A component names at most one transparent container, since `transparent_container` returns one `Symbol`. A tuple return is a `MethodError` (no `convert` to `Symbol`) when the build makes `TransparentContainerUnknown`.
rows.note: No diagnostic exists for two names; declare.jl:344 records the case as unrepresentable. A defect fix would have `_check_transparent` refuse a non-Symbol return as a diagnostic.
